turns.text: Already running before the crack finishes bouncing off the grating underfoot — three strides gone before the sound catches up to the body making them. behind: wet boots, closing fast, faster than any two-legged chase has business closing. ahead: the walkway thins to a rail with nothing under it but sixty feet of neon-stained rain. legs stop asking permission and just go.

the overpass shudders under six boots instead of four paws — Sector 9 colors, soaked through, closing the gap one hard stride at a time. rain needles in sideways off a transit sign stuttering PUNCTUAL◇TRAVEL◇GUARANTEED through a dead pixel cluster. below, the street runs a river of red taillights that won't slow down for anything that falls into them. the rail ahead simply ends. the next platform sits eleven feet out across open air.

No room left to spend on hesitating — front paws catch the rail's lip and the whole body follows into the jump, ears flattening hard against the wind funneling up from the street. midair there's nothing left to correct with, only the shape of a landing already decided before it happens. claws find the far platform's edge a half-breath before the rest of the body arrives, and it's ugly, and it holds.

old rivets take the impact with a jolt that rattles up through steel plating never built to be a runway. behind, at the gap, the chase stalls — one of the three leans out over the rail, cursing a jump none of them are built for. a security drone answers a page nobody sent, rotor spinning to life two levels up, its spotlight beginning a slow, bored sweep across rooftops and walkways alike. ahead, the platform runs down into shadow — an underpass strung with cable, and along its far roofline, shapes that don't move like pigeons.

Ears track that roofline without the head turning toward it — one shape sits apart from the rest, too still, angled wrong for anything with feathers, two small circles of reflected light where eyes ought to just be dark. it doesn't come closer. it doesn't need to. the fur along the spine lifts anyway, and the paws pick the opposite direction without stopping to justify it.

good instinct — that ledge isn't one worth crossing tonight. mirrored lenses catch the drone's spotlight sweep and throw it back flat, cold, unblinking, a silhouette that's held that exact rooftop corner longer than the corner's had a name. it doesn't move. it doesn't have to. the spotlight slides past without pausing, the way light sometimes just knows better than to ask questions. below, the underpass mouth opens dark and dry, humming faint with current nobody up top is supposed to be able to reach.

/\/\_/\/\
    (  O   O  )
     \  ^Y^  /
      )=====(      -- ears up, rotor incoming --

Down into the dry dark before the spotlight finishes its arc — paws finding cable bundles instead of concrete, stolen current humming warm under each footfall. breath comes back in ragged pulls now that there's a roof overhead again. one foreleg throbs where the landing wasn't as clean as it needed to be, and the tongue goes to it without being told to.

the underpass swallows sound the way the open street never does — engine-roar and rain reduced to a distant wash, replaced by the low industrial hum of cable runs feeding half the district's off-book rigs. the air tastes like ozone and warm plastic. somewhere close a NekoCorp jingle bleeds thin and warped through a busted speaker, the same six notes looping wrong, over and over, like even the tape's given up caring.

The throbbing paw gets three licks and no more — no time to spend on it here. a length of cable sheathing further along shows fresh incisor marks, deliberate, testing something in the insulation by taste rather than by hunger. the smell of teeth and copper lingers over it, recent, careful, gone before it could be caught at it. further down, past a gap in the corrugated wall, low voices trade something back and forth in a rhythm that isn't quite talking and isn't quite silence either.

a doorway sits cracked open there, spilling a thin wash of screen-light and cigarette smoke into the tunnel — chips changing hands across an upturned crate, encrypted decks dealt facedown, somebody laughing too loud at a joke that isn't funny outside that room. none of it's worth lingering for. the passage keeps running, dry and humming, toward a wider chamber where the ceiling opens up into a gutted transformer housing radiating actual heat.

A different scent cuts through the cable-hum and copper — scorched fur, old smoke baked permanently into it, laid down heavy enough to mark the whole stretch as somebody's. not fresh, not threatening, just there, the way a scar is there. ears flick toward it and then away. whoever left it isn't close tonight.

that trail belongs to a resident of the gutted lot two blocks over, what used to be an apartment block before the demolition crews and the holographic parking lot that replaced it overnight. lives in the vents now. bites drones for sport, or spite, or both — the district doesn't much care which. the scent's old enough to mean safe passage, not an argument. ahead, the transformer housing hums its steady note, dry and warm, exactly the kind of ledge a body could stop needing to run on.

The ledge takes the weight without complaint, warmth soaking up fast through a coat gone flat and dark with rain. eyes stay open longer than strictly necessary — old habit, the rule that sleep comes last, after everything else has been accounted for.

the transformer keeps its low steady hum, an indifferent lullaby for anything smart enough to use it. outside the underpass mouth, Sector 9's boot-fall has long since faded back into the traffic wash, and the rooftop silhouette — if it was ever really watching at all — is gone now too, leaving nothing behind but a faint trace of ozone where mirrored lenses might have caught a spotlight, once, for exactly as long as it needed to.

Ears fold flat, half in rest, half still listening out of habit. the ache in the foreleg settles into something filed away rather than something urgent. dry, warm, unbothered — for now, and for now has always been the only length of time worth counting on.

morning's still hours off, but the rain's thinning to a mist against the grate overhead, and the underpass keeps its secret the way it always does — quiet, humming, lit by nothing but a stolen router's patient blink and whatever gray light the storm lets leak through. the city doesn't sleep. it just goes quieter, breath by breath, waiting for the next thing to come running through it.
